solutions.check: 28 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Cider's off – drunk by stupid nit with healthy bank balance?

indicators.note: a drink that has gone off is spoiled, so its letters are spoiled into a new order
something stupid is muddled, so these letters come out muddled
what is drunk by someone goes inside them, so one piece is swallowed by another

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A fool, flush with money, gulps down cider that has gone bad.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate scrambles happen here, and 'drunk by' then puts one inside the other; 'stupid' does double duty as the surface insult.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a positive balance, money held rather than owed, is what being in credit at the bank means.

clue.text: see 27ac.
Casual chat after crack results in dubious, snide headline

indicators.note: something done casually is loose and haphazard, so these letters fall into a careless order
coming after something means following it, so this piece is placed second

blocks.note: to have a crack at something is to have a go
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Idle gossip after a breakthrough ends up as a sneering, questionable newspaper headline.
explanation.walkthrough: GOTCHA was the Sun's notorious 1982 front page on the sinking of the Argentine cruiser Belgrano, a favourite target of Private Eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sun's infamous Falklands front page made the word a byword for gloating tabloid splashes.

clue.text: Scornful of Bill's turned back doodah

indicators.note: turning something back makes it face the other way, so the letters run right to left

blocks.note: AC, short for account, is a bill; with the 's it becomes ACS
a doodah is a whatsit, a thing whose name escapes you

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at Bill, whose gadget has been turned round the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: AC is the standard abbreviation for account, a bill; the possessive 's comes along with it before the turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Scathing remarks are bitterly contemptuous ones, the same harsh disdain that scornful describes.

clue.text: The bloke rats out 'suit'

indicators.note: letters that are out are disordered or put out of place, so they need rearranging

blocks.note: a bloke is referred to as he
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A man in a suit is exposed as a grass, ratting on colleagues.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks around 'suit' hint that it is not clothing: it is one of the four suits in a pack of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearts is one of the four card suits alongside spades, diamonds and clubs in a standard deck.

clue.text: Ten pisspoor MPs collectively having nothing to lose, rave

indicators.note: something pisspoor is badly done, so these letters are badly arranged
what you lose you no longer have, so a letter drops out

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
MPs together make up the House of Commons
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O; it is taken out

explanation.surface: A useless bunch of MPs with nothing to lose rant and rage.
explanation.walkthrough: TEN is shuffled to ENT; HOUSE loses its O to make HUSE, and the two join as ENTHUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To enthuse is to speak with great excitement, gushing about something, which matches raving about it.

clue.text: Deeds prepared, incorporating outskirts of Cambridge, and withdrawn

indicators.note: the outskirts of a place are its edges, so only the outer letters are kept
something prepared has been worked over and made ready, so its letters are reworked
to incorporate is to take into the body, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
the first and last letters of the city

explanation.surface: Property deeds are drawn up on the edge of Cambridge, then quietly pulled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deeds' reads as legal documents, but it is simply raw letters; the scramble happens before the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: To secede is to formally leave a union or federation, so having seceded is having withdrawn from it.

clue.text: It hurts, being collared by Cruz – affected emotionally

indicators.note: to be collared is to be grabbed round the neck, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: Ted Cruz is a Republican US senator from Texas
the cry you make when something hurts

explanation.surface: Someone grabbed by Senator Cruz feels the pain and is shaken up.
explanation.walkthrough: Cruz's first name is the key: TED wraps round the cry of pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Being touched means feeling moved or stirred inside, an emotional response to kindness or sadness.

clue.text: Boris's role purportedly makes him perspire

indicators.note: to make is to construct or form, so these letters are built into something new

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Rumour has it that Boris Johnson's job leaves him sweating.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a whole-clue joke about a leader under pressure, but the last two words hold exactly the letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Johnson's job was leading the government, and that position is the office of Prime Minister.

clue.text: (& 18ac.) A firm control of groin stimulation by hack

indicators.note: stimulation stirs things up, so these letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
to hack at something is to rip or tear it

explanation.surface: A seedy tabloid tale of a journalist getting a firm hold below the belt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' looks like the journalist doing the stimulating, but here it is the verb meaning to tear.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding something in an iron grip means unyielding, tight control, the idiom for firm authority.

clue.text: Coach manipulated a uretic travesty

indicators.note: to manipulate is to handle and work something into a new shape

blocks.note: a railway coach is a carriage, or car
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A trainer has twisted something into a grotesque mockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' looks like a person who manipulates; it is the railway carriage. 'Uretic' is a real word, relating to urine, chosen to supply letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A caricature is a grotesquely exaggerated imitation, and a travesty is likewise an absurd distorted version.

clue.text: Supplement rear with, er, appendage

blocks.note: to supplement is to add
the rear is the back end
both are hesitation noises

explanation.surface: An embarrassed hesitation while discussing some extra rear appendage.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'er' reads as a hesitation in the sentence, but it is fodder: another hesitation sound replaces it.
explanation.definitionFit: An addendum is extra material attached at the end of a document, something appended to it.

clue.text: Sun hacks author – inappropriate

indicators.note: hacking means breaking into a system, so one piece breaks into another

blocks.note: Kingsley or Martin Amis, father and son novelists
S is the abbreviation for sun

explanation.surface: The Sun newspaper hacks a writer's phone, which is improper.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the tabloid phone-hacking scandal; the Sun is only the letter S, slipped in before AMIS's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something amiss is out of order or wrong, which covers behaviour judged improper or unsuitable.

clue.text: see 25ac.
On sticking end of todger into fish, cut back

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept
sticking something into another thing pushes it inside

blocks.note: re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading
a tench is a freshwater fish
the final letter of the word; a todger is British slang for a penis

explanation.surface: A smutty image of a member being stuck into a fish, then pulled back out.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking 'on' to mean 'about', as in a memo heading, is a standard crossword convention; 'cut back' is the definition, not a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrench is to reduce spending or economise, the same as making cuts or cutting back.

clue.text: Democrat study causes disquiet

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for Democrat
to read a subject is to study it

explanation.surface: A report from the Democrats leaves people uneasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Study' looks like a noun, a report; it is the verb, as in reading history at university.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread is anxious fearful apprehension, a stronger form of the unease that disquiet names.

clue.text: Gloomy and sad as an old failed Republican presidential candidate?

definitions.text: as an old failed Republican presidential candidate
definitions.note: cryptic: full of Dole, like him

blocks.note: first meaning: mournful, woebegone

blocks.clueFragment: as an old failed Republican presidential candidate
blocks.note: second meaning, read cryptically: Bob Dole lost the 1996 US election

explanation.surface: Is a beaten Republican presidential hopeful as miserable as he looks?
explanation.walkthrough: Bob Dole was the Republican nominee beaten by Bill Clinton in 1996; the question mark flags the punning second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A doleful face or tone is mournful and woeful, expressing the same sorrow as gloomy and sad.

clue.text: see 10ac.
Reveal Kitty's been recruited by online newspaper

indicators.note: someone recruited is taken into an organisation, so one piece is taken inside another

blocks.note: the Indie is the nickname of the Independent, which has been online-only since 2016
a kitty is a cat; the 's is 'has'

explanation.surface: A newspaper announces that someone called Kitty has joined its staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kitty' looks like a woman's name but is the pet, and 'Kitty's' reads as 'Kitty has'. The Independent, a British national paper, is nicknamed the Indie.
explanation.definitionFit: To indicate something is to point it out or make it known, which is to show or disclose it.

clue.text: Smooth material occupied one's seat?

definitions.note: read as two words, SAT IN

blocks.note: first meaning: a glossy woven fabric
second meaning, split in two

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark warns that the second meaning needs the word broken into two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Satin is a silky fabric with a glossy face, prized for its sleek feel; sat in is simply being seated.

clue.text: Conceited – and a bit of a drip?

definitions.note: a phrase describing something, where the answer is an adjective

blocks.note: first meaning: stuck-up, snooty
second meaning: a runny nose drips, covered in mucus

explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit of a drip' usually means a feeble person; the question mark points to the literal drip from a cold-ridden nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Snotty means arrogant and superior in informal speech, and literally means running with nasal mucus.

clue.text: Space organisation broadcast the ruin of Eden

indicators.note: what is broadcast goes out over the air, so we go by the sound

blocks.note: NASA, the American space agency, said out loud

explanation.surface: A space agency's broadcast tells of paradise lost in Genesis.
explanation.walkthrough: Eden is not the garden but Anthony Eden, British Prime Minister, whose premiership collapsed after the 1956 Suez crisis against Egypt's President Nasser.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasser's nationalisation of the Suez Canal led to the failed invasion that forced Eden's resignation.

clue.text: Sun, sex, top off, naked ... leads to complete absence of company

indicators.note: taking the top off removes the head, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: Sol is the Latin name for the sun
it is a coy word for sex
naked means nude; it loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A holiday of sunbathing, sex and going topless and nude ends with being left all alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top off' looks like part of the topless sunbathing, but it beheads the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Solitude is the state of being alone without other people, a total lack of companionship.

clue.text: Member's circle in attempt to get Boris overturned

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it
overturning something flips it, so the letters run the other way in a down light

blocks.note: an attempt is a try
the letter O is a circle
Boris Johnson was Prime Minister

explanation.surface: A Member's inner circle plots to topple Boris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member's' is 'Member is', with Member as the definition; it was Conservative MPs who forced Johnson out in 2022.
explanation.definitionFit: A Conservative MP is a Member of Parliament, so Member describes the person accurately.

clue.text: Fed up, or in the sack sporting an erection

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it

blocks.note: the sack is slang for bed
taken as written
rigid with arousal

explanation.surface: A bedroom quandary: is he bored, or aroused?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or' looks like a joining word offering alternatives, but it is fodder that goes inside BED.
explanation.definitionFit: Bored stiff is the idiom for being thoroughly weary and uninterested, completely tired of something.

clue.text: (& 14ac.) Mercury, say, is unstable next to black stuff

indicators.note: placing one thing next to another sets them side by side

blocks.note: something unstable sways back and forth, the four-letter verb also meaning a large stone
tar is thick black stuff

explanation.surface: A science note: the element mercury is volatile beside something black.
explanation.walkthrough: Mercury is not the metal or the planet but Freddie Mercury, the singer of Queen; 'say' signals an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Freddie Mercury, frontman of the band Queen, is a famous example of a celebrated rock musician.

clue.text: One who keeps going at it – needs second heart!

definitions.text: One who keeps going at it

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
ticker is slang for the heart

explanation.surface: A tireless lover needs a spare heart to keep going.
explanation.walkthrough: The innuendo of 'keeps going at it' is the joke; the definition is just someone persistent.
explanation.definitionFit: A sticker is a persevering person who sticks at a task and refuses to give up.

clue.text: (& 2dn.) Toxic chemical agent that's a threat to the world

indicators.note: something toxic is poisoned and corrupted, so these letters are corrupted into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A poisonous chemical weapon endangers the whole planet.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description rather than a synonym, made fair by the surface about global danger.
explanation.definitionFit: Global warming caused by greenhouse gases is widely regarded as a grave danger to the planet's future.
